question: Previous searches chose one new expert at a time. Can training feedback assign small weights to several complementary experts without sacrificing the established research pair?
fit: Reuse exact frozen probabilities from the previously registered 27 candidates and the three typed TabICL configurations. Fit a nonnegative linear probability pool by cross-entropy with L2 shrinkage on the challenger shares and on their sum. Keep at least half the probability weight on the incumbent (aligned tree and TabICL). Use penalties .0005, .005, .05. On each development rotation, use only its other five-fold training side, split again into three group-stratified folds, fit all three penalty choices, choose among those within one standard error of the best cross-entropy the largest penalty. Admit a fitted mixture only if its cross-fitted training accuracy beats the incumbent by at least .003, at least two of the three inner folds improve, and its cross-entropy also improves. Fit the selected coefficients on the entire decision-training portion for assessment. Count every numerical optimization as an actual router fit.
assessment: Reuse the six outer rotations seeded 583257 of the 2432 feedback rows; each is excluded from fitting its own decision. Save each decision and each outer prediction before reading outer scores for reporting. Compare the automatically admitted or retained result and the unguarded diagnostic with the incumbent. A prospective cold-solver experiment requires at least .003 aggregate held gain and at least four nonnegative folds. These are reused development rows, not a course grade. No additional base-model fit or API.
